Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Slopball browser published-party restore

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
Shell
REPLAY_SLOPBALL_PARTY_RESTORE_OUT=/absolute/fresh/output \
  nix develop --command bash tests/replay_slopball_party_restore/run.sh

Three browser players and an observer publish a scored, moving owner-streamed match. Every source browser is SIGKILLed, with the exit signal checked. An independent Odin reader decodes the actual service checkpoint, including complete world validity, score, names, body scopes/samples, tick, digest and ball pose/momentum. The service is then SIGKILLed and reopens its existing database with creation disabled.

The observer registers first and must remain without authority. The host restores the exact saved world in epoch two; its first eligible actual solver seed must match the independent archive's position, angle, linear velocity and angular velocity. The other players reclaim seats two/three. Continued play requires a new kick and goal plus new scoped body observations. Named observer chat, guest save refusal, a common world digest and independently decoded publication two are checked.

RTC bytes, graphics traces, disjoint control rectangles and absence of browser-local save slots are checked. All actions use the ordinary UI/game methods. The bridge only observes the game; no checkpoint or synthetic world is installed by the fixture.

execute.py WEB_BUILD SERVICE_BUILD FRESH_OUTPUT reuses prepared exports. verify/ reads source/continued publications. Source browser profiles, service SQLite data and credentials are private; archive redacted events and receipts only. These loopback runs do not establish Internet deployment, cross-device physics or preservation of solver contact caches and every live tick after publication.

The runner executes both original-creator and trusted-seat-two restoration. Use RSL_RESTORE_OWNER=host or striker with the execute helper to select one case. In the latter, the creator remains absent until seat two restores the published world and solver momentum, then rejoins seat one. Continued publication is checked against the selected authority seat and publisher; the new authority must kick and score for its own team. Guest publication remains refused.
